observations: Two photos show an open shipping container/truck bay filled with many disassembled car engines/engine parts (multiple cylinder heads, blocks, intake/exhaust components, pulleys, timing-related parts).
No complete vehicle is shown; no VIN plate, no dashboard, no exterior body, no odometer, no engine running footage.
The photos do not show any readable model badge/engine code/label that ties the parts to a specific Lexus/Toyota model.

claims.evidence: Photos show mixed engine parts; no readable RX350/Lexus identification.
No ES350 identification visible in photos.
No IS250 identification visible in photos.
No Camry identification visible in photos.
No shipping documents, container markings, or Belgium-related labels visible.

claims.claim: Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened.
claims.evidence: Photos show engines/parts already disassembled; no test video, no compression/leakdown results, no mileage proof, no seal/lock evidence.

risks.risk: The item may not be a complete, matching engine (could be mixed parts or incomplete assemblies).
risks.proof: A photo/video of the exact engine assembly in one piece (or a full parts list) with matching engine code/label and all components accounted for.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as incomplete/unknown condition (worst case: not guaranteed to run).

risks.risk: Wrong model/engine family (RX350/ES350/IS250/Camry engines differ; parts shown could belong to different variants).
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the engine identification plate/engine code stamped on the block (and/or VIN/engine code from the donor).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as wrong/uncertain fit (worst case: buyer may not be able to install without major sourcing).

risks.risk: “Never opened” contradicts the visual evidence of disassembly.
risks.proof: Photos of factory seals/torque marks and a clear view of the engine internals showing whether it was previously opened (plus a test report).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as previously opened/unknown internal condition (worst case: needs rebuild).

risks.risk: “Tested and working / no knock” is not verifiable without running proof.
risks.proof: Short video of the engine running from cold start (or a dyno/diagnostic printout with scan tool readings).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven running (worst case: treat as not working).

risks.risk: Potential damage during shipping/handling (bent rods, cracked housings, missing sensors/bolts).
risks.proof: Close-ups of critical areas (block casting, crank pulley area, cylinder head surfaces) plus a checklist of included sensors/ancillaries.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as may have damage/missing parts (worst case: additional parts and labor required).

proof_requests: Send clear close-up photos of the engine code/ID plate stamped on the block (and any label) so the exact variant can be confirmed.
Send a photo/video showing the exact engine as a complete assembly (or confirm it’s a full engine vs mixed parts) with all major components present.
Provide running proof (cold start video) or diagnostic/test report showing no knock and health readings.
Provide mileage proof (donor info/VIN or auction sheet) and photos of seals/lock marks to support “never opened.”
List exactly what is included (starter, alternator, ECU, sensors, timing components, intake/exhaust manifolds) with photos of each.
response.reason: The photos show multiple disassembled engine parts with no readable engine/model identification and no running/test evidence. The seller’s claims about model, mileage, and working condition are not verifiable remotely, so the correct item and worst-case condition can’t be priced confidently yet.
